reason: The whole point of axis B: the candidate is a different viewer, so this field must differ.

MapLibre counts zoom for 512px tiles and Leaflet for 256, so the same view is MapLibre zoom 3 and Leaflet zoom 4. Since D34 both viewers round a fit down to viewer.zoomSnap, so the scale is the same. One viewer.location.zoom in a Config still means two scales. Normalising it moves every Host config and every saved bookmark, so it needs a ruling, not a patch - CONTEXT.md 8.1.

A viewer modifier beside the neutral class. Both viewers now render smk-minimap, which is what a Theme selects on; smk-minimap-leaflet and smk-minimap-maplibre are extras for anything that must tell them apart. D9: converge on viewer-neutral, keep the modifier.

mode is a MapLibre-only tool - the support manifest says so. In Leaflet the shared half still builds, so the tool exists and is disabled and not visible. That is the documented no-viewer-half case, not a fault. See CONTEXT.md 8.2.

The class component.ts puts on a tool whose visible flag is true. It is here because mode is visible in MapLibre and does not exist in Leaflet - see the ModeTool toolState ruling. Not a chrome difference of its own.

The default BC basemap through two client libraries. esri-leaflet-vector reads the VectorTileServer description first; MapLibre goes straight to resources/styles/root.json and takes the tile template from there. Both draw the same map. D9 wire behaviour: each Viewer uses its own native call.

The D17 item through two client libraries. esri-leaflet-vector reads the item description and moves the sprite to cdn.arcgis.com; MapLibre reads the item style from the CDN and takes the sprite from www.arcgis.com, where the style points. Same files, same map. D9 wire behaviour.

The D17 hillshade source. esri-leaflet-vector keeps the source url, so MapLibre inside it reads the service description as TileJSON; the MapLibre viewer uses the tile template the style gives. Both fetch the same hillshade tiles - 8 each at zoom 6 over the Coast Mountains, measured 2026-09-17. D9 wire behaviour.

esri-dynamic. Both viewers now call /export - that was the 2026-09-07 fix. esri-leaflet asks for JSON and then fetches the image the service produced under arcgisoutput/; MapLibre uses the export url straight as a raster tile template. Same endpoint, two client strategies. Leaflet also sends dpi=96, which is the service default.
The Leaflet side of the same esri-dynamic export. See the _ags_map ruling.
esri-leaflet reads the service description before it exports. See the _ags_map ruling.
Registration order. It reaches both viewers, so it only shows here when one pane starts a tool the other does not.

esri-feature. Both viewers fetch the features now - that was the 2026-09-07 fix; before it, the Leaflet layer threw at creation and never drew. esri-leaflet tiles its feature queries, so it sends eight /query calls with resultType=tile; MapLibre fetches once with where=1=1. Same service, two client strategies. D9 wire behaviour.

dist/smk.es.js calls require() for the ESRI 3D viewer modules at load, whichever viewer runs. A host page that does not load the ArcGIS API - as one that never wanted the 3D viewer would not - gets this once. Measured 2026-09-07 and recorded in CONTEXT.md 8.1; the host-contract test guards it so it cannot grow.

The Leaflet minimap keeps smk-spacer beside the neutral smk-minimap, because SMK 1.0 rendered it and a class a Host can see is a contract (D9). MapLibre never had one. The neutral class is what a Theme selects on.

Decision D22, and wire behaviour (D9). esri-leaflet-vector reads the VectorTileServer description first; the MapLibre viewer reads the item style from cdn.arcgis.com and takes the tiles straight from it.
Decision D22, wire behaviour (D9). esri-leaflet-vector reads the item description from www.arcgis.com; the MapLibre viewer does not need it.
Decision D22. The MapLibre inside esri-leaflet-vector notes a large bucket in one Esri World Topographic tile. It draws. Informational.
The mode widget, a MapLibre-only tool (see the ModeTool toolState ruling). Leaflet drew a disabled 2D button that did nothing; it now sets showWidget false and draws none.
The same mode widget as smk-mode-tool, by its tool id.
The 2D/3D label inside the mode widget, as smk-mode-tool.
The mode widget's status class, as smk-mode-tool. No other tool has a 2d status.
